title: A Centenary of Justice -- Ch. 7: Employee Participation During the Centenary
primary_topics: Chapter 7 of 'A Centenary of Justice' -- a Valentine's Day tribute (February 14, 2001, Court of Appeals Auditorium) in which CJP honors the rank-and-file officials and employees of the Supreme Court, Court of Appeals and Department of Justice as those 'closest to the heart' of the institution

A survey of employee-focused centenary programs spearheaded by the Centenary Executive Committee's Employees' Participation Committee -- health, sports, cultural, welfare and recognition activities affirming that the workforce is central to judicial dispensation
The mass housing program for judicial employees (negotiated with PAG-IBIG for favorable rates) as a major centenary highlight

The thesis that an institution 'can be effective only when it has the support and the cooperation of the people composing it' -- the men and women of the judiciary as 'the most important components' of the centennial
sub_topics: The Valentine's framing (delivered partly in Filipino): the celebration was deliberately set on February 14 to stress that 'the closest to the heart of the Supreme Court' are the employees who serve justice
Context of broad employee participation: Region 7's two-day Cebu celebration (Jan 26-27, ~1,000 officials and employees) and the Dumaguete grand debate (Feb 9, with 800 paying P50 each)
The cultural presentation managed by the Cultural Committee under Justice Minerva P. Gonzaga-Reyes

Employee health and welfare programs: a Basic Life Support Training Course (Sept 21, 2000), a Cancer Awareness seminar-workshop (Nov 9, 2000), the Employees' Sports Festival (Nov 17), and a Pfizer-coordinated seminar on 'Sexual Dysfunction Among Lay People' (Dec 7) run by the SC Clinic and Employees Association
Future activities by the Employees' Participation Committee (Attys. Luz Puno and Marissa Villarama): a blood-letting program (Feb 23) and seminars on stress management and the dangers of smoking

Recognition: loyalty awards (monetary awards and certificates) for employees with at least ten years' service, and the Search for Special Centennial Awardees for Excellence under a committee of Justices Josue N. Bellosillo and Jose Y. Feria

The mass housing program for judicial employees under a sub-committee headed by Justice Bernardo P. Pardo -- sites inspected and PAG-IBIG negotiations for favorable interest rates similar to those given policemen

The closing thesis: 'without our employees, we cannot speak of the judiciary'; an office 'can be effective only when it has the support and the cooperation of the people composing it,' so employees are 'the most important components' of judicial dispensation and the centennial

stances.claim: The rank-and-file employees -- not only the magistrates -- are 'the most important components of judicial dispensation,' because 'without our employees, we cannot speak of the judiciary,' and any office 'can be effective only when it has the support and the cooperation of the people composing it.' Institutional greatness rests on its ordinary workforce, not merely its officials.
stances.rhetorical_move: institution-as-its-people: inverting the usual hierarchy of attention to place the rank and file at the center of the centennial, dramatized by deliberately holding the tribute on Valentine's Day
stances.confidence: asserted as the governing sentiment of the employee tribute

notable_anecdotes: The Valentine's Day choice: CJP explains (in Filipino) that the celebration was deliberately set on February 14 to underscore that those 'closest to the heart' of the Supreme Court are the employees who serve justice.

The breadth of employee programs: from a Basic Life Support course and a Cancer Awareness workshop to an Employees' Sports Festival and even a Pfizer-coordinated seminar on 'Sexual Dysfunction Among Lay People,' with stress-management and anti-smoking seminars and a blood-letting drive to follow.

The mass housing program: a centerpiece centenary benefit -- a sub-committee under Justice Bernardo P. Pardo inspected sites and negotiated with PAG-IBIG for favorable interest rates 'similar to those given to policemen in their mass housing program.'

Loyalty and excellence awards: monetary awards and certificates for employees with at least ten years' service, plus a nationwide Search for Special Centennial Awardees for Excellence chaired by Justices Bellosillo and Feria.

one_paragraph_summary: Chapter 7 of 'A Centenary of Justice' reproduces a Valentine's Day tribute CJP delivered on February 14, 2001 at the Court of Appeals Auditorium, deliberately timed (he explains in Filipino) to stress that those 'closest to the heart' of the Supreme Court are the rank-and-file employees who serve justice. Setting it amid broad employee participation -- Region 7's two-day Cebu celebration (Jan 26-27, ~1,000 staff) and the Dumaguete grand debate (Feb 9) -- he catalogues the Centenary Executive Committee's employee-focused programs: a cultural presentation under Justice Minerva P. Gonzaga-Reyes; health and welfare activities run by the SC Clinic and Employees Association (a Basic Life Support course, a Cancer Awareness workshop, an Employees' Sports Festival, and a Pfizer-coordinated seminar on 'Sexual Dysfunction Among Lay People'); upcoming blood-letting, stress-management and anti-smoking seminars organized by the Employees' Participation Committee (Attys. Luz Puno and Marissa Villarama); loyalty awards for ten-year veterans; and a Search for Special Centennial Awardees for Excellence chaired by Justices Bellosillo and Feria. A major highlight is a mass housing program for judicial employees under a sub-committee headed by Justice Bernardo P. Pardo, with PAG-IBIG negotiations for favorable interest rates 'similar to those given to policemen.' His governing thesis is that the employees are 'the most important components of judicial dispensation' -- 'without our employees, we cannot speak of the judiciary,' and any office 'can be effective only when it has the support and the cooperation of the people composing it' -- and he closes by inviting everyone to relax and honor, in his Filipino words, all who serve the justice of the nation.
